#1780. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1779. Michael Carrick, Man Utd break unwanted all-time records after sacking confirmed with club statement

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:17

Michael Carrick has officially been sacked as Manchester United head coach and has departed Old Trafford with an unwanted all-time record.

The 45-year-old’s inevitable exit was confirmed on Thursday morning with a club statement explaining why the “extremely difficult” decision was made.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025-26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

“The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Four months after becoming Man United’s interim boss following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim, Carrick was rewarded with the permanent role in May after steering the club back into the Champions League.

However, Carrick has now left Man United sitting in 18th place in the Premier League table following the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years, accumulating only eight points from their opening 10 games (W1 D5 L4).

Although Red Devils supporters have continued to give their full backing to Carrick, acknowledging that deeper issues lie with the club's hierarchy, the decision has been made for the club to move in a new direction.

Carrick has therefore set an unwanted record of overseeing the fewest games as a permanent Man United manager (32 in total, 16 as permanent boss), overtaking Clarence "Lal" Hilditch (33) who was in charge between October 1926 and April 1927.

Across those 32 games, Carrick won 15, drew eight and lost nine in all competitions (46.9% win rate), though he only recorded four victories across his final 16 matches in charge (25% win rate).

Meanwhile, Man United have now sacked two managers (Carrick in November and Amorim in January) in the same calendar year for the first time in their 148-year history.

Carrick’s exit also means that the Red Devils have sacked managers in three successive seasons for the very first time.

Prior to the dismissals of Carrick and Amorim, Erik ten Hag was relieved of his duties in October 2024, just four months after being given a new contract.

Man United have had a total of seven permanent managers and five different interim bosses since club icon Sir Alex Ferguson called time on his legendary 26-year reign in the summer of 2013.

It is widely expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as Carrick’s successor, with an agreement in principle said to be in place for him to swap his current role as USA national team coach for the Old Trafford hotseat.

#1778. ‘Not ready’, ‘out of control’ and ‘the end of the world’: What Amorim’s words tell us about Milan’s state

Ruben Amorim is not one to hold back when it comes to speaking his thoughts to the media, and the last few days are no exception.

The past week or so has seen Amorim have to digest the best and worst of his AC Milan side. The 3-1 derby win over Inter generated a euphoria that begun whispers of the word ‘Scudetto’, before a dismal defeat to Ferencvaros which saw Milan drop to 29th in the Europa League standings.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This rollercoaster of extremes didn’t stop either side of those two games either. Before the victory over the Nerazzurri a 2-1 lead had been coughed up against Bologna, who scored three times in the second half to win at San Siro and inflict the first league defeat on the Rossoneri.

Yesterday, the Diavolo responded to the season low-point against the Hungarians by beating a Genoa side that had won their last three games and four of their last five. This Milan team is a very difficult one to work out, and it seems even the manager is struggling to do so.

After the Ferencvaros and Genoa games, we learned a lot about where Amorim sees his team to be at. Some key lines from his post-match comments demonstrated a wide spectrum of reaction, from anger to pride, passing through encouragement and worry.

Ruben Amorim has often gone to bat for his players after negative performances and results this season, but it seems that the defeat on Thursday night had pushed his patience to the brink as he tore into his team after the game.

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire,” he said.

“We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight. I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

For the first time we saw a peek behind the mask, one that has very often been one portraying an optimistic and positive expression. Amorim knew there was no point attempting to lie to the supporters, the media but above all to himself.

What we know is that Amorim echoed the ferocity of these sentiments when speaking in the dressing room after full-time in what was likely the first dressing down that the team got. Six players were reported to have disappointed more than the others, too.

Above all, what stood out was the fact that the head coach opted to question whether his players wanted it enough. This was no longer a question of learning an identity, rotation or an injury crisis: it became a matter of heart.

Another intriguing extract from the post-Ferencvaros tirade that Amorim went on was about the squad’s ability to balance playing in two different competitions, namely Serie A and the Europa League.

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

Once again, Amorim offered a bit of a revelation: the league is the absolute priority for Milan this season. It may not exactly be revolutionary information, given that a top four spot remains the most accessible avenue to the main objective for 2026-27: securing a Champions League return.

And yet, in his emotional outburst, the former Sporting CP and Manchester United boss told us all in black and white that Serie A will be the focus. As a result, it’s right to expect more ups and downs in Europe, especially with such a depleted squad.

There is an element of observational realism about Amorim’s words; almost an admission of defeat in his attempts to spin two plates at the same time and get the most out of the resources at his disposal. Does it suggest a Europa League resurgence is coming? Not exactly.

Amorim has not made a habit of mentioning individuals ever since his arrivals, both in his pre-match words but especially after games in which emotions are running high. However, he brought up someone who was absent for the Ferencvaros game.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses, we should have won even with those who started,” he said.

Going into the season there were some who were legitimately questioning whether Strahinja Pavlovic would even be a tactical fit for Amorim’s usual 3-4-2-1 system, given that he prefers more composed, ball-playing outside centre-backs.

The answer to those doubts is that in November the Serbian has become the shining light in the eyes of his manager. We mentioned earlier that it had become a question of heart, and nobody can doubt that Pavlovic has that in abundance.

For all of the talk about tactics, systems, shapes and patterns, football is a simple game that very often comes down to who wants it more. In this regard, Amorim elevated Pavlovic as the example to follow, while hoping he returns from injury for the Frosinone game after the break.

Moving on to the post-Genoa reflections, what was quite apparent was that Ruben Amorim was in no mood to get carried away. In fact, if anything, he revealed his belief that his team are still miles off where he wants them.

“What I feel is that, when we’re competitive, we’re difficult to beat, and now we’re steering the game towards our style. We push for control with the ball.

“When we’re not able to be competitive, we’re completely out of control. It’s a big difference, but it’s something we need to work on. But again, the team’s evolution, the way we’re playing, is completely different from the start of the season, and I’m happy with that.

“We should have more points. I’m clearly not happy with the European games, not just because of the results, but because of the performance. Results can happen, but the performances are far from what we want. However, I think we’ll be a better team in the future.”

So, for now this version of Milan is not one that satisfies the coach. The words are a good summary of what the last six games have shown, in which there have been an even split of victories and defeats: on their day the team can beat anyone in the league, but on an off-day they can lose to anyone too.

What Amorim seems keen to hammer home is that progress for this season will be judged on the ability to bring the ceiling closer to the floor. In other words, we have seen the potential of this team already with some impressive wins, yet the base level for performances remains frighteningly low.

Consistency is not just about being able to string together several positive results in a row, something the current Rossoneri do not seem capable of. It is about the repeated displaying of an idea and an identity every few days, to suggest the team are getting closer to the vision the coach has.

Various things make that difficult (perhaps unachievable, based on Amorim’s other comments) right now, such as the injury situation and the multiple windows needed to sculpt the squad. Progress is not always linear, but the target has been set.

One of the themes that Amorim has been consistently questioned on this season is how to unlock the club-record signing Goncalo Ramos, who remains stuck on three goals (one of which was a penalty).

After the Genoa game, he said: “I think we’re lacking time in the final third. We control the ball away from the opponent’s penalty area. This is also key for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault.

“Pulisic is far from the penalty area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area. All these players play away from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

This is one of the points of ‘evolution’ that Amorim clearly wants to see from his side, but is yet to achieve. Milan are not yet a team that can sustain pressure in the opposition half, nor can they penetrate the box with any regularity either.

In fact, a report from Sky backed this up with some interesting numbers, look specifically at data per 30 minutes of actual possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. When the Rossoneri have the ball, it is rarely in a threatening area.

With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of, and it makes the positive attacking numbers (23 goals in 11 league games) feel quite unsustainable.

The Portuguese striker meanwhile is first in the Milan squad in Serie A for interceptions, recoveries, touches in the middle third and touches in the opposition half. He is second for receptions, touches and duels, and third for passes.

Simply put, the No.9 is being drawn away from the area he should be operating in because the team are not capable of sustaining spells of possession further up the field, so he needs to drop deeper to feel involved.

This is something Amorim must work on, because while the goals are coming from other sources for now – in some cases due to the space Ramos helps create – it could all come tumbling down unless the attacking play improves more generally.

🚨🎙️🛡️ Ruben Amorim on Gonçalo Ramos: “Ramos is helping US more than we are helping him. It’s a TEAM problem, not a Ramos problem.”

“We don’t spend enough time in the final third.”

“When we start keeping the ball there more often, Gonçalo is going to score MANY goals.” pic.twitter.com/b3Zs6YxNym

— Milan Wire (@MilanWireX) November 8, 2026

Finally, we end with what was perhaps the most passionate part of Amorim’s comments following the win at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris on Sunday, again centred around the levels he expects from his team.

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like we did on Thursday and then turn it on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

In many ways, the manager was speaking in a way that channels how fans have experienced the past week. How is it possible that Milan can be completely outplayed by a side sat third in the Hungarian lead just days after convincingly beating the Italian champions?

Against Genoa, how can the team play as they did in the first half, and then appear to completely drop off a cliff in the second half when the time came to dig deep and bring the result home? The disparity in levels both in-game and from match to match is astounding everyone, even the man in charge.

What Amorim said about wanting his side to fear losing was particularly poignant. In his time at the club so far he has repeatedly stressed that feeling of responsibility to honour the red and black shirt and all that comes with that, including the importance of results.

Some may argue that encouraging an ‘end of the world’ type mentality will not help the players play more carefree and will actually only stiffen them up. Yet, it could also provide the stimulus for the fight and the courage that Amorim clearly so desperately wants.

There is a hint of irony about the ‘no days off’ comment, as Amorim has given the squad a one-week break, at least those who were not called up by their national teams. When everyone reconvenes there will be another crucial stretch of games to see out the year, starting with a home match against the surprise package Frosinone.

For all of the energy, passion and emotion that Ruben Amorim speaks with, it will eventually be time for words to become deeds. Consistency must be not a distant mirage but some thing tangible that emerges.

Only then will a full buy-in be achieved and patience be awarded. Otherwise there will always be the fear that darkness follows light.

#1777. Kosovo vs Israel - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 12 Nov 2026 12:34

Kosovo and Israel will clash at Stadiumi Fadil Vokrri on Saturday afternoon in UEFA Nations League B Group 3.

The hosts are second in the standings with five points from four games, while the visitors are at the bottom of the table with two points after four matches.

Kosovo got their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign underway with a deserved 1-0 victory over Ireland, with captain Vedat Muriqi scoring the late winner.

Franco Foda's side had dominated the encounter, holding 57% possession, taking 22 shots and creating 2.74 expected goals (xG) compared to Ireland's three efforts and 0.25xG.

Foda would have been looking for his team to build on that triumph in the following matches, but Kosovo have failed to win any of the subsequent three fixtures.

Kosovo suffered a 3-1 defeat to Austria on matchday two, followed by back-to-back draws with Israel (0-0) and Austria (1-1), leaving them second in the standings with five points, only ahead of third-placed Ireland thanks to their head-to-head record.

Ahead of a potentially pivotal matchday six encounter with Ireland, when both teams could be fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A, Kosovo will be eager to secure all three points on Saturday - especially as Ireland face leaders Austria.

Kosovo, despite failing to score, were in control of large periods of their 0-0 draw with Israel, and a return to their home ground for the reverse fixture will provide a considerable confidence boost.

Isreal also head into this encounter having failed to win any of their four League B Group 3 fixtures, suffering two defeats and recording two draws.

Ran Ben Simon's side, as a result, sit fourth in the standings with two points, trailing the third and fourth-placed sides by three points with two games remaining.

Israel will, therefore, have to secure a victory on Saturday and hope for results to go their way on the final day if they are to avoid having to compete in the relegation playoff fixture.

Israel will draw confidence from each of their two goals scored in League B Group 3 having come away from home, although they have conceded four goals in those two away games.

Israel have, however, failed to beat Kosovo in any of their three clashes, suffering one defeat and recording two draws, conceding twice and scoring only once in those matches.

Captain Muriqi and Edon Zhegrova have scored two of Kosovo's three goals, and both are expected to start alongside Baton Zabergja in attack on Saturday.

Fisnik Asllani is Kosovo's only other goalscorer in the Nations League this campaign, and the forward will provide an option from the bench for Foda.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Bleon Kurtulus could be awarded his debut, potentially starting alongside Ilir Krasniqi and Ron Raci as part of Kosovo's back three.

Meanwhile, Israel are likely to start Oscar Gloukh and Liel Abada behind Dor Turgeman in attack, while captain Dor Peretz should start in the centre of a midfield three.

Further back, Roy Revivo and Ilay Feingold will provide width from full-back, with Nikita Stoinov and Eli Dasa in central defence.

Saipi; Kurtulus, Krasniqi, Raci; Vojvoda, Avdullahu, Hodza, Gallapeni; Zhegrova, Muriqi, Zabergja

Tzur; Feingold, Dasa, Stoinov, Revivo; Gandelman, Peretz, Azoulay; Abada, Gloukh; Turgeman

Kosovo have had the stronger campaign and have never lost to Israel in any of their previous meetings, and with the home advantage also in their favour, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

#1776. Mauricio Pochettino should not take Man Utd job - unless two 'needed' signings are made

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:38

Gary Neville has warned Mauricio Pochettino against becoming the next Manchester United head coach unless he is promised two new signings in January.

It was confirmed on Thursday morning that Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties just six months after his permanent appointment, with the Red Devils revealing in a statement that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

The man expected to replace Carrick is former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss Pochettino, who reportedly has an agreement in principle to swap his current role in charge of the USA national team with the Old Trafford hotseat.

Pochettino, 54, is set to take over a Man United side languishing inside the Premier League relegation zone following the club’s worst start to a season in 40 years.

The struggling Red Devils have looked particularly vulnerable in defence, conceding 19 goals across their opening 10 league games – only Ipswich Town (20) and basement club Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Ahead of Pochettino’s expected arrival, former Man United defender Neville believes that the Argentine should be assured by the club’s hierarchy that he can make at least two defensive signings in January before accepting the manager’s job.

Speaking on The Overlap, Neville said: “If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven.

“He'll do that with a pay-off, so do that in your contract, but secondly, he needs two defenders in January, so he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

“They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.”

Neville added: “He's got to insist on the way in that there's some sort of transfer control, some form of budget there that he knows he can meaningfully change the team.

“Mauricio, I don't think is the kind of manager either who would say 'Give me half a billion' - I don't think he's that type of guy, I think he's someone who is a bit more responsible and will look at things.

"He'll want to bring players through and he'll want to develop young players - I get that and he'll do that. I just think he needs to protect himself in these next 12 months with the transfer budget. He has to.

“The only time you can insist upon it is at the very beginning and he needs two defenders in January.”

Neville, who made 602 appearances for Man United and is regarded as one of England’s greatest right-backs, did not hold back on his criticism of the Red Devils’ current defensive options.

“I mean look at the back four that he finished with on Sunday (4-4 draw with Aston Villa). It was [Diogo] Dalot left-back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,” Neville added.

“That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.”

Man United have been linked with a plethora of defenders throughout this calendar year, but their top left-back target Lewis Hall signed a long-term contract extension at Newcastle in September, seemingly ending their pursuit of the Englishman.

Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Rennes starlet Mahamadou Nagida are among a number of other left-backs who have been linked with Man United.

The likes of Roma’s Wesley, Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, Brentford’s Nathan Collins and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are other defenders who are believed to be on the Red Devils’ radar ahead of the winter window.

Pochettino could be announced as Man United’s new manager before the club travels to Anfield for their next Premier League match against Liverpool on November 22.

#1775. Odegaard confident Norway will get Wales back

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Norway's Martin Odegaard is out for revenge when his team host Wales in a crunch Nations League fixture.

Wales beat Norway 2-1 in October, with Dan James and Neco Williams sealing a memorable win at Cardiff City Stadium.

That is one of three defeats Norway, who reached the World Cup quarter-finals, have suffered across their Nations League Group A4 campaign.

Norway have suffered as many defeats in their last three matches (three) as they suffered in their previous 23 games combined in all competitions (W17 D3 L3). They have not lost four in a row since October 2016.

It means they must beat Wales in Oslo on Saturday to stand a chance of progressing to the last eight.

But Odegaard feels Stale Solbakken's team are well set to get one back on Wales.

"Our level was not where it should be. I think it's probably the only game for a long time where we haven't been playing to our standards," he said.

"Wales is a good team, a competitive team, lots of good players in big leagues and a physical team as well, and we were prepared for that.

"But I think on the day we were just not showing up to our standards, and that's something we want to show [on Saturday], and we can do a lot better. We want to show a different version."

A post shared by Herrelandslaget (@herrelandslaget)

Since a 0-0 draw with Switzerland in March, all 12 of Norway's matches in all competitions have seen both teams score.

Norway have conceded two or more goals in each of their last five outings. It is their longest run without a clean sheet since an 18-game streak between June 1980 and June 1982, and their worst run of shipping 2+ goals since March 1976 (six games).

And with Wales in the same boat as Norway when it comes to needing a win to keep their quarter-final hopes alive, Solbakken is anticipating a fierce test.

"It's like a boxing [match], going head-to-head, fist-to-fist," said Solbakken.

"I think Wales has always been a very attacking team under Bellamy. They've had great progress with the ball.

"I think it suits the team with the offensive players they have, the speed on the wings and Harry Wilson back. And [Lewis] Koumas getting more minutes for Liverpool, so I think that suits them.

"I'm not surprised that they will go all in, but it's our home game, so obviously I think they will also have their struggles with us. Let's see."

#1774. GdS: Milan ready €50m January assault for Tresoldi to give Ramos a partner – the strategy

AC Milan are serious about signing Nicolo Tresoldi from Club Brugge, with an attempt being readied ahead of the winter window.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan intend to sign another striker even before the summer arrives, in order to boost their Champions League hopes. The name that they have chosen is someone the fans already know well: Nicolo Tresoldi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

At the end of June, the club announced the signing of Gonçalo Ramos for over €70m, the most expensive signing in the club’s history to date (and likely for a while to come). Ramos hasn’t – at least for now – cured Milan’s goal-scoring deficiency in the No.9 role.

The negotiations for Tresoldi, however, are shaping up to be costly. Last summer, Club Brugge rejected another Italian offer of €35m from Roma, and in the meantime the price has skyrocketed after the forward bagged 13 goals in 15 games.

Adding his four goals this season against Germany’s youth team brings him close to 20 for the season already. His league hat-trick against VV Sint-Truiden at the end of October followed his hat-trick at San Siro against Inter, marking the night that every Rossoneri fan knew his name.

Therefore, the cost could now be around €50m, another huge expense if Milan really decide to go all-in. The club made a €24m loss in the last accounts after three years of profit, and the temptation is to speculate to accumulate, i.e. to invest more and make sure of the Champions League revenues.

There’s a desire to finalise the deal as early as the January transfer window, unless Brugge move to raise the price, perhaps due to a potential foreign competition. Milan believe that their relationship with the Belgian side is actually strong, with Gerry Cardinale ready to lead talks again.

As for Ramos, the investment so far has yielded just three goals and two assists, which doesn’t mean he wasn’t effective and is ready to be shelved, but it’s precisely when paired with another striker that the management believes the Portuguese could be more productive.

In short, a two-striker team can’t be ruled out in the future, with Tresoldi alongside the former Benfica man. In the European race goals fuel the climb, and Milan know this after last season’s late collapse, keen to avoid it again.

Should Milan hit a wall erected by Club Brugge, they would leave the Tresoldi option open for the summer. In the meantime, they would fill the gap with a striker on loan from a top European club.

However, Tresoldi could provide an initial assist for Milan: his support for the Rossoneri is well-known and has been publicly stated, so among the various options available, Nicolò would choose the San Siro.

A permanent return to Italy could also benefit coach Roberto Mancini, who – after the Under-21 European Championship (which Tresoldi will compete in with Germany) – would finally like him to play for the senior Azzurri side.

Nicolò, born in Cagliari in August 2004, is still free to choose which (senior) national team he wants to represent, and Mancini expressed his confidence earlier this week: “I spoke to Tresoldi, and Ranieri spoke to us too. First of all, I think he needs to feel the desire to play for Italy.

“He was born in Italy, like his father [former defender Emanuele], who played for the Under-21s and won the European Championship. I think there’s a chance he’ll choose the Azzurri. He knows he can be an important player for our future, and I hope he makes the right choice.”

#1773. 'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026

Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

Pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’

Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season

Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss

Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they said. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’

'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'

Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'

To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’

Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He says his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football

Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books

‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’

#1772. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

“When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1771. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage: Club statement and update on ‘advanced talks’ with successor

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:19

Crystal Palace have announced that Pierre Sage has been relieved of his duties as head coach.

The 47-year-old has departed Selhurst Park less than five months after he was appointed the successor to Oliver Glasner, who had steered the Eagles to Conference League glory last season and a historic first FA Cup triumph the year before.

Sage arrived at Palace on the back of a successful 2025-26 campaign in charge of Lens, who finished second in Ligue 1 and won their first-ever Coupe de France trophy.

However, the Frenchman was unable to make an immediate impact in South London and has left Palace sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of his opening 10 games (W1 D2).

A 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool last weekend represented a fourth consecutive top-flight defeat for the Eagles that proved to be the final nail in the coffin for Sage, who saw his side concede a division-high 24 goals.

Palace also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League standings with only one win from their first four games on the board thus far.

Frank de Boer (five) is the only permanent manager in Crystal Palace’s 121-year history who has overseen fewer matches than Sage (16), who departs with a 31.25% win ratio (W5 D3 L8).

Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager. The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/JcVHA6FIhe https://t.co/VAM8XnpHlq

In a club statement released on Thursday, Palace said that three members of Sage's backroom staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - had also left the club.

The Eagles added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

"An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course."

It is now understood that Sage already has a new managerial job lined up, with a 'verbal agreement' said to be in place.

It was reported at the end of last month that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage as Palace head coach.

The likes of Anthony Barry – Thomas Tuchel’s assistant coach at England - Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, multiple reports, including one from BBC Sport, claims that Thomas Frank is now in ‘advanced talks’ to take over.

It is thought that Palace wish to finalise Frank’s appointment before their next Premier League game away against Coventry City on November 21.

Frank has been out of work since he was sacked as Tottenham Hotspur boss in February, after less than eight months in charge.

The 53-year-old, who replaced Ange Postecolgou, won only 13 of his 38 games at the helm and left the North London club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

During a brief, trouble-filled spell in charge, Frank was unable to earn the backing of the Spurs faithful, with his tenure defined by numerous setbacks and awkward blunders including drinking from a coffee cup branded with the Arsenal badge.

However, Frank had enormous success at previous club Brentford during a memorable seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, guiding the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a competitive top-flight team, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

The Dane won 132 of his 317 games in charge of Brentford and they finished as high as ninth in the Premier League under his tutelage in the 2022-23 season.

Frank stated in June that he had no intentions of taking a new job and opted to conduct media and punditry duties during the 2026 World Cup, but he now appears to be ready to jump back into management and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

#1770. MN: Why Milan and Inter are calm despite Council request over new stadium plan

A potential obstacle has already arisen after the Generali Stadium announcement, even if all parties remain calm for now.

As MilanNews recall, Tuesday morning’s edition of Corriere della Sera carried a report that had everyone on edge, just days after the renderings of the project were published. However, by the afternoon some quite important clarifications had arrived from Mayor Giuseppe Sala.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The newspaper reported that the Milan City Council had approved a bipartisan measure to halt the current environmental assessment process for the Generali Stadium project and request a new one that encompasses all the interventions the two clubs intend to undertake.

This includes the demolition of the current stadium once the new stadium is operational. The goal is to make the green light for the work conditional on a prior Health Impact Assessment (HIA).

MilanNews have learned that the City Council’s motion is non-binding, meaning Mayor Sala’s administration will not be obligated to follow the council’s request. More importantly, it does not suspend the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

The two clubs remain calm regarding the next phases, especially since the SEA and the VIS are two separate and distinct phases that must both be addressed before work on the new stadium can begin.

The Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a procedure established by Italian and European legislation that evaluates the environmental sustainability of a plan or program prior to its approval.

It differs from the subsequent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), which instead examines the environmental effects of a specific project prior to its potential authorisation and implementation.

The Council has therefore advanced a request that would not currently be foreseen under normal formal procedures. In any case, the two clubs are confident in the material produced, providing even more than necessary by integrating the Environmental Report with all the health-related details currently available.

Milan and Inter have no intention of avoiding any type of assessment. On the contrary, the EIA is scheduled for early 2027, by spring, with completion expected within a few months. Further investigations into the project and its impacts will therefore be undertaken shortly, as per the timetable.

Yesterday afternoon, Mayor Sala issues a statement on the news that broke, once again emphasising that the project will move forward.

“It’s clear that continuing to call the stadium issue into question is a gift to the right. I don’t want us to delude ourselves into thinking we’ve already won. I respect the City Council’s opinion, but the Council will respect the fact that I have no intention of reconsidering,” he said.

“We’ll discuss it in the City Council, but I have no intention of reconsidering the stadium. We’ve been talking about it for three years; everyone should do what they think best. I will continue to be consistent, and I will try to move forward with the stadium project.”

Councillor Martina Riva also gave a comment to MilanNews too: “Small obstacles? They won’t be a problem, we are convinced of the validity of our operation and we will move forward: the city, the teams and the fans who want a fully accessible stadium deserve it.

“I really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectationsaccessibleI really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectations.”

#1769. How Pep Guardiola feels about USA job after Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd manager update

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 13:22

The USA national team would like to appoint Pep Guardiola as their new manager to succeed Manchester United-bound Mauricio Pochettino, according to a report.

The Red Devils officially confirmed the sacking of head coach Michael Carrick on Thursday and it is understood that an agreement in principle has been reached for Pochettino to take the reins at Old Trafford.

Man United are said to have made contact with the USA and are willing to pay the £7.4m release clause in Pochettino’s contract, though the Red Devils would be comfortable with him taking charge of international matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

USA would have ideally liked to have retained the services of Pochettino, who was appointed head coach in September 2024 and oversaw the country’s 2026 World Cup campaign before signing a contract extension in August to keep him in charge until the summer of 2030.

However, The Athletic reports that former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City boss Guardiola is expected to become a ‘top target’ for the USA national team in the event that Pochettino moves to Man United.

Their pursuit of Guardiola would not be straightforward, though, as the Catalan has shown little interest in an imminent return to management since ending his legendary 10-year career at the Etihad Stadium in the summer.

Guardiola turned down the opportunity to become Italy head coach earlier this year, with the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malago, telling La Repubblica: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

Nevertheless, Guardiola is said to have previously had dialogue with USA, and has long been intrigued by the possibility of working in America.

Guardiola was allegedly contacted by USA, along with Jurgen Klopp, before they ended up hiring Pochettino to replace Gregg Berhalter in 2024.

Speaking about USA after Pochettino was appointed, Guardiola told reporters: "The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and be able to get the national team to the next step.

“The potential with the USA is there, given the number of people and sports, and so on.

"I wish [Pochettino] and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager, an experienced manager."

Following his 2012 departure from Barcelona, Guardiola spent a year-long sabbatical in New York City, living with his family in a luxury apartment near Central Park where he enjoyed a rare sense of anonymity.

After a decade in charge of Man City – where he won 20 trophies including six Premier League titles – Guardiola has since become a Global Ambassador for the club and stated how he plans to take an extended break from management.

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025. "I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he added: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure. When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all.”

As well as the USA, Guardiola has been tipped to manage England at some stage in the future, though Thomas Tuchel is currently in charge of the Three Lions and is expected to stay at least until the end of the 2028 European Championship.

#1766. Man Utd managers since Ferguson: Every manager's record, win percentage and time in charge

By Calum Burrowes | 12 Nov 2026 13:48, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:21

Manchester United are expected to confirm Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, who has been relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

The former Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur boss is expected to leave his role with the United States to take charge of the 20-time English champions, with another managerial change set to begin a new chapter at the club.

Since Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, United have appointed a succession of permanent managers and interim coaches, with varying degrees of success.

Here, Sports Mole looks at every manager to take charge of the Red Devils since Ferguson's departure, examining their time in charge, overall record and win percentage.

David Moyes was selected to succeed Ferguson in July 2013 after impressing during his time at Everton, but his spell at Old Trafford proved considerably more difficult than anticipated.

The Scot won the Community Shield in his first competitive fixture, beating Championship side Wigan Athletic 2-0, but United struggled for consistency throughout the season.

Moyes was dismissed in April 2014 after the club's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League had faded, with United eventually finishing seventh in the Premier League.

Now 63, the Scottish manager is back at Everton for a second spell on Merseyside, having returned to the club in January 2025.

Record: 51 matches, 27 wins, 9 draws, 15 defeats

Following Moyes's departure, former United midfielder Ryan Giggs took temporary charge for the final four matches of the 2013-14 season.

Giggs won two, drew one and lost one of those fixtures, including a 4-0 victory over Norwich City.

His brief spell gave him a 50% win percentage, but he was not retained as the club's permanent manager.

Record: 4 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat

Louis van Gaal arrived in the summer of 2014 after guiding the Netherlands to the World Cup semi-finals in Brazil, bringing considerable managerial experience to Old Trafford.

The Dutchman won 54 of his 103 matches in charge and secured the FA Cup in his second season, beating Crystal Palace in the final.

However, United's failure to qualify for the Champions League proved costly, and Van Gaal was dismissed in May 2016, just two days after lifting the trophy.

Record: 103 matches, 54 wins, 25 draws, 24 defeats

"The Special One" became United's third permanent manager since Ferguson in May 2016, going on to record the highest win percentage of any permanent appointment since the legendary Scot's departure, with 84 victories from 144 matches at a rate of 58.3%.

The Portuguese enjoyed a successful first season, winning the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League, before guiding the Red Devils to second place in the Premier League in 2017-18.

However, results and performances deteriorated during his third campaign, and he was dismissed in December 2018.

Record: 144 matches, 84 wins, 32 draws, 28 defeats

Former United striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer initially arrived as caretaker boss in December 2018, enjoying an impressive run of results before being handed the job permanently.

Across 168 matches, Solskjaer recorded 91 wins, 37 draws and 40 defeats, giving him a win percentage of 54.2% and cementing his status as one of the most popular managers among United fans since Ferguson's departure.

United reached the Europa League final  in 2021 and finished second in the Premier League that season, but a poor run of form during the following campaign led to his departure in November 2021.

Record: 168 matches, 91 wins, 37 draws, 40 defeats

Carrick took temporary charge following the Norwegian's dismissal, overseeing three matches between November and December 2022.

The former Tottenham and England midfielder won two and drew one, leaving him unbeaten during his first brief spell and with a win rate of 66.7%.

He subsequently left the club's coaching staff following the appointment of Ralf Rangnick and went on to manage Middlesbrough before returning to Old Trafford earlier this year.

Record: 3 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Ralf Rangnick was appointed interim manager in December 2021 and was expected to oversee a transition before moving into a consultancy role at the end of the season.

However, his time in charge proved difficult, with United winning just 11 of their 29 matches, drawing 10 and losing eight.

His 37.9% win percentage was the lowest of any manager to take charge of the club since Ferguson at that point.

Ralf Rangnick has since spent over four years in charge of Austria, guiding the national team to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Record: 29 matches, 11 wins, 10 draws, 8 defeats

Erik ten Hag arrived in May 2022 and made an encouraging start to life in Manchester, winning the League Cup in his first season and restoring the Red Devils to the Champions League.

The Dutchman recorded 70 victories in 128 matches, giving him a win percentage of 54.7%, and added the FA Cup to his trophy collection in 2024.

Nevertheless, inconsistent league performances and a poor start to the 2024-25 campaign resulted in his dismissal in October 2024.

Record: 128 matches, 70 wins, 23 draws, 35 defeats

Van Nistelrooy stepped in as caretaker boss following Ten Hag's departure, having previously served as part of the Dutchman's coaching staff.

The former United striker made an immediate impression, winning three and drawing one of his four matches in charge.

His 75% win percentage is the highest on the list, although his spell was considerably shorter than those of the club's permanent appointments.

Since leaving the Red Devils, Van Nistelrooy has gone on to manage Leicester City, but was dismissed after winning just five of his 27 matches in charge of the Foxes.

Record: 4 matches, 3 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Amorim was appointed in November 2024 after impressing at Sporting Lisbon, but his time at Old Trafford proved challenging despite arriving with a strong reputation.

The Portuguese won 24 of his 63 matches, recording a win rate of 38.1%, and struggled to establish consistency during his time in charge.

His spell ended in January 2026, with United having failed to make the progress expected.

Record: 63 matches, 24 wins, 18 draws, 21 defeats

Former United midfielder Darren Fletcher was placed in temporary charge following Amorim's departure in January 2026.

Fletcher oversaw two matches, drawing one and losing the other, before the club turned to Carrick.

His short spell therefore ended without a victory.

Carrick returned to Old Trafford in January 2026, initially taking charge until the end of the season after United dismissed Amorim, who is currently in charge of AC Milan.

His second spell began impressively, with 12 wins from his first 17 matches helping the Red Devils secure a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to Champions League football.

Carrick subsequently signed a new contract in May, but his fortunes changed dramatically during the 2026-27 campaign.

United struggled for consistency and found themselves in the relegation zone after 10 league matches, with their dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa proving to be Carrick's final fixture.

The club confirmed his departure on November 12, bringing his second spell to an end less than six months after he signed a new deal with the club, leaving United 18th in the league.

Record: 32 matches, 15 wins, 8 draws, 9 defeats
